claims.evidence: The Azure Architecture Center pages Database services on Azure and AWS (ms.date 2026-10-05) and Google Cloud to Azure services comparison (ms.date 2026-04-08) were read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at a pinned commit; AWS and Google documentation was not reachable from the authoring environment, and no experiment was run because cloud services were not available.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: Amazon RDS maps to Azure SQL Database, Azure Database for MySQL and Azure Database for PostgreSQL (select by engine first); Aurora Serverless maps to Azure SQL Database serverless with different scaling and billing models; DynamoDB maps to Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, both partitioned by key with different consistency, indexing, query, transaction, capacity and pricing models; Amazon DocumentDB maps to Azure DocumentDB or Cosmos DB for MongoDB; Amazon Keyspaces maps to Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra or Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra; Neptune supports property graph and RDF while Cosmos DB for Gremlin supports property graph only; ElastiCache maps to Azure Managed Redis; Amazon MemoryDB is a durable primary database with no direct Azure equivalent, and Azure Managed Redis should not be the authoritative store; a compatible API does not guarantee feature or operational parity.
claims.section: Amazon RDS and Azure relational database services; Non-relational database services; Service comparison
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: Cloud SQL maps to the Azure SQL family and Azure Database for MySQL and PostgreSQL; Cloud Spanner, in the row horizontally scalable relational database, maps to Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL and to Azure Database for PostgreSQL with elastic clusters; Cloud Memorystore maps to Azure Managed Redis.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: The source states: A cheat sheet of cloud database services with open-source or third-party options; Google has limited documentation for database use cases, so some entries may not be accurate.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung dòng tra (quan hệ; tài liệu, khóa–giá trị, cột rộng; đồ thị và bộ nhớ đệm) và một khung bốn điều bảng tra không nói. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source is an image table that the lesson does not reuse; the table is rebuilt from two Azure Architecture Center comparison pages and limited to the rows they contain.
The lesson adds the caveats those pages attach to each row: API compatibility is not parity, MemoryDB has no direct equivalent, graph scope differs, and Spanner is mapped across models.
